Estimate moments of the conditional response distribution

Source: R/moments.R
fitted_moments.Rd

Calculate population moments at observed or supplied covariate values, with uncertainty propagated jointly through the model's distribution parameters.

Usage

fitted_moments(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
fitted_moments(
  object,
  data = NULL,
  moments = c("mean", "variance", "cv"),
  uncertainty = c("delta", "simulation", "none"),
  ci_level = 0.95,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  nuisance = c("estimated", "fixed"),
  n_draws = 10000L,
  seed = NULL,
  scores = NULL,
  method = c("gaussian", "mh", "inla", "user"),
  draws = NULL,
  envir = NULL,
  family_index = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted mgcv::gam() or mgcv::bam() model.

...

Prediction arguments passed to mgcv::predict.gam(), including exclude and na.action. type, newdata, se.fit, and terms are controlled internally and cannot be supplied.

data

Optional prediction data. With NULL, evaluate fitting rows, retaining fitting offsets and the model's missing-value convention.

moments

Character vector selecting "mean", "variance", "sd", "cv", "skewness", "kurtosis", or "excess_kurtosis". "all" requests all seven. CV is SD divided by a strictly positive mean; kurtosis is the fourth central moment divided by squared variance.

uncertainty

One of "delta", "simulation", or "none".

ci_level

Coverage of pointwise uncertainty intervals, between 0 and 1.

unconditional

Include smoothing parameter uncertainty when available.

nuisance

One of "estimated" or "fixed". The default propagates uncertainty in estimated family parameters outside the coefficient vector, such as Gamma dispersion, negative-binomial shape, or Tweedie power. "fixed" explicitly conditions on their fitted values.

n_draws

Number of joint parameter draws for simulation, at least two. User-supplied coefficient draws determine their own count when omitted.

seed

Optional integer random seed. An explicit seed preserves the caller's random-number state; NULL uses and advances it when generating random draws. Supplied draws do not consume random numbers.

scores

Optional numeric category scores, in category order, for ordinal or multinomial models. Otherwise return moments of each category's zero/one membership indicator. Binomial moments describe a Bernoulli response, independently of fitting trial counts or likelihood weights.

method

Coefficient sampler for simulation; see post_draws(). Joint sampling of estimated global family parameters uses "gaussian".

draws

Optional coefficient matrix for method = "user", in fitted coefficient order. Requires nuisance = "fixed" if global parameters were estimated outside the coefficient vector.

envir

Environment used to recover model covariates.

family_index

Optional integer component-family positions for grouped predictions, one per supplied row. Membership is otherwise recovered as in fitted_samples(). It must agree with membership recoverable from data.

Value

A tibble of class "fitted_moments", containing .row, covariates, .parameter, .fitted, .se, .lower_ci, .upper_ci and .status. Category indicators include .category; multivariate responses include .y; grouped responses include .family. Simulation also includes .p_defined. All estimates, standard errors and interval bounds are on the requested quantity's scale.

Details

Estimates describe one response at each covariate combination, with unit observation weight. Fitting weights are not transferred to new responses. For ML/REML fits with an estimated dispersion, all uncertainty modes use the likelihood estimate stored in reml.scale. The conditional coefficient covariance is rescaled to this value. This can differ from mgcv's separate Pearson/Fletcher estimate in sig2; the saved outer Hessian describes the likelihood estimate, so combining it with sig2 would mix estimators. Response variance and uncertainty in its estimate are different quantities: .fitted contains the variance when .parameter is "variance", and .se describes uncertainty in that estimate. These are not moments of a posterior predictive mixture or prediction intervals for future observations.

Standard Gaussian, Poisson, binomial, Gamma and inverse-Gaussian families, negative binomial, beta, scaled t, Tweedie, all seven location/scale/shape families, ordinal, multinomial and multivariate-normal models are supported. Censored normal, logistic and Poisson families return moments of the latent uncensored response. Beta moments describe the beta likelihood, without the epsilon clipping used by some response generators. bcg() supports the original lognormal response only when its Box-Cox parameter is fixed at zero: other powers require a distribution outside the inverse transformation's domain that the fitted family does not specify. Quasi and Cox families are unsupported. Grouped (gfam) predictions use each row's component family and the full joint model covariance. Grouped ordinal components require explicit category scores; grouped category-indicator output is unsupported.

The delta method differentiates the complete parameter-to-moment transformation and uses its full joint covariance. Gaussian, Poisson, Gamma, inverse-Gaussian and Tweedie derivatives (including their models with several predictors) are analytic; other families use central numerical differences. Positive variance, SD, CV and kurtosis intervals are calculated on a log scale; .se always remains on the reported quantity's scale. Other delta intervals use the identity scale. Simulation uses joint parameter draws and equal-tailed quantiles. Both methods retain the moment evaluated at fitted parameters as .fitted.

With estimated global family parameters, a first-order joint Gaussian approximation combines the conditional Bayesian coefficient covariance with second derivatives of the ML/REML fitting criterion and derivatives of the fitted coefficients with respect to the family and smoothing parameters. Without unconditional, outer curvature is conditioned on smoothing parameters. With unconditional, the full saved outer Hessian is inverted, including its smoothing uncertainty. The curvature and coefficient sensitivities are evaluated at the fitted parameters, with mgcv's mapping for linked or fixed smoothing parameters. A positive-definite Hessian is required. This does not also add the corrected coefficient covariance, which would count that uncertainty twice. The fitted object must store a matching Hessian and sensitivities; unsupported fitting methods, including fast REML BAM fits, give an error. This is a local approximation about the fitted parameters, not an exact posterior sampler for dispersion or family shape. With fixed global parameters, the existing coefficient covariance or post_draws() machinery is used. Delta intervals and Gaussian simulation with unconditional = TRUE and fixed estimated global parameters use the first-order smoothing correction conditional on those fixed parameters: native corrected covariance can also include their uncertainty. This requires the same saved outer Hessian and sensitivities when smoothing parameters are present. Legacy negbin() fits outside ML/REML require explicit nuisance = "fixed"; use nb() to estimate and propagate shape uncertainty. The covariance calculation uses a first-order expansion of the coefficient means and does not include mgcv's additional correction for changes in the conditional coefficient covariance. The moment_info attribute records which approximation was used.

Nonexistent moments are retained as NA with a status and one warning per call. In simulation, .p_defined records the fraction of draws with a finite value. Intervals and standard errors are withheld if any draw is undefined; draws are never silently dropped. CV requires a positive mean, and skewness and kurtosis require positive variance. GEV moments of order r require shape < 1/r; t moments require degrees of freedom greater than their order. Status values distinguish "moment_does_not_exist", "nonpositive_mean", "zero_variance", "undefined_in_draws", and "missing_predictors". "numerical_failure" identifies a value that could not be calculated with finite precision or invalid distribution parameters; "derivative_unavailable" identifies a finite estimate whose local derivative could not be calculated.

See also

conditional_moments(), fitted_values(), fitted_samples()

Examples

library("mgcv")
m <- gam(mpg ~ s(wt, k = 5), data = mtcars, method = "REML")
fitted_moments(m, data = mtcars[1:3, ], moments = c("mean", "variance"))
#> # A tibble: 6 x 18
#>    .row .parameter .fitted   .se .lower_ci .upper_ci .status   mpg   cyl  disp
#>   <int> <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1 mean         23.0  0.707     21.6       24.4 ok       21       6   160
#> 2     1 variance      7.12 1.84       4.29      11.8 ok       21       6   160
#> 3     2 mean         21.2  0.662     19.9       22.5 ok       21       6   160
#> 4     2 variance      7.12 1.84       4.29      11.8 ok       21       6   160
#> 5     3 mean         25.3  0.766     23.8       26.8 ok       22.8     4   108
#> 6     3 variance      7.12 1.84       4.29      11.8 ok       22.8     4   108
#> # i 8 more variables: hp <dbl>, drat <dbl>, wt <dbl>, qsec <dbl>, vs <dbl>,
#> #   am <dbl>, gear <dbl>, carb <dbl>
fitted_moments(m, data = mtcars[1:3, ], moments = "variance",
  uncertainty = "simulation", n_draws = 500, seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 3 x 19
#>    .row .parameter .fitted   .se .lower_ci .upper_ci .status .p_defined   mpg
#>   <int> <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1 variance      7.12  1.91      4.14      11.1 ok               1  21  
#> 2     2 variance      7.12  1.91      4.14      11.1 ok               1  21  
#> 3     3 variance      7.12  1.91      4.14      11.1 ok               1  22.8
#> # i 10 more variables: cyl <dbl>, disp <dbl>, hp <dbl>, drat <dbl>, wt <dbl>,
#> #   qsec <dbl>, vs <dbl>, am <dbl>, gear <dbl>, carb <dbl>
